foremon.guide.0.title: Getting started
foremon.guide.0.body:
Craft a Work Whistle: two gold ingots with a string above the right one. Right-click any chest with it to turn that chest into a job site. Pick a job on the left, click one of your party Pokemon at the bottom to put it to work (or open the PC tab to pick from any PC box), then press Start. Workers live in your PC while they work, so they are always safe. Click a worker to send it home.

A job site chest has a gold frame and its job icon turning above it, so you can tell it from an ordinary chest. Grey means paused.

Need more room? Hold the whistle, sneak and right-click other chests to add them to the site as extra chests (blue frame, chain icon). Workers use them as one big storage.

Right-click the air with the whistle to open this screen again.
foremon.guide.1.title: Jobs
foremon.guide.1.body:
Lumber: chops natural trees around the chest and replants saplings. Player-built log walls are left alone.

Mining and Demolition: hold the whistle, sneak and right-click two corners to mark the area. Mining keeps what it digs up; Demolition gives the blocks back.

Sorting and Hauling: sneak and right-click other chests to link them. Sorting tops up chests that already hold an item; Hauling fills any linked chest.

Farming: crops, nether wart, berries and apricorns.

Smelting: needs fire. No furnace or fuel required.

Building: see the Building page.
foremon.guide.2.title: Who is good at what
foremon.guide.2.body:
Every Pokemon gets a star rating for every job. Hover over a Pokemon in a job site to see exactly why: its stats, its types, its ability, the moves it knows, its size and its nature all count.

There are no tools. What a Pokemon can mine comes from its level, and Rock, Ground and Steel types dig one tier harder.

Some places need the right Pokemon: high blocks need one that can fly, blocks under water need one that breathes water, blocks by lava need a fire-proof one. Field moves help too: Cut fells a whole tree at once, Dig takes a whole ore vein.

Level perks: every job has perks a Pokemon unlocks as it levels up. A lumberjack first learns Leaf Sweep (the leaves of a felled tree vanish), then Timber in stages until whole trees come down in one swing. Miners learn Vein Miner, farmers Wide Harvest, and so on. The Perks tab shows every ladder and where your party stands.

The Work Dex tab shows your best Pokemon for each job and lets you look up any species.
foremon.guide.3.title: Filters
foremon.guide.3.body:
Every job site has a filter. In "only these" mode workers only touch what is on the list; in "all except these" mode they touch everything else. An empty list means everything.

Open the Filter tab and click items from your own inventory to add them, or use the groups such as Ores and Logs. The skill tree gives more filter slots.
foremon.guide.4.title: Building
foremon.guide.4.body:
Install Litematica, load a schematic and place it where you want it, as you normally would. Select that placement in Litematica, then open a job site and press Load Litematica. The placement must be inside the job site's work area.

Put the materials in the chest. Workers build from the bottom up, putting torches, doors and other attached blocks on after what they hang from. If something runs out the site says what is missing and waits.
foremon.guide.5.title: Rest and food
foremon.guide.5.body:
Working uses stamina. A worn-out Pokemon falls asleep for a while, then carries on. Berries in the chest wake it up straight away, so a stocked chest keeps a crew going. Friendship raises how long a Pokemon can work.

Working slowly raises your Pokemon's friendship and gives them a little EXP. Each Pokemon also ranks up in the jobs it does, from Novice to Master, getting faster each rank.
foremon.guide.6.title: Skill tree
foremon.guide.6.body:
Everything your Pokemon do earns Work XP. Spend it in the Skill Tree tab. You start with one chunk of work area, one worker and one job site; everything can be upgraded.

Foreman: work area, crew size, job sites, linked chests, filter slots, remote control, night shift.
Labour: speed for every job, tree felling, vein mining, bonus ore, double harvests, twin furnace, master builder.
Care: stamina, shorter rests, better berries, mastery, friendship and EXP from work.
Logistics: carrying, moving faster, longer links, item pick-up, restocking.
foremon.guide.7.title: Problems
foremon.guide.7.body:
If a worker gets stuck it hops next to its target, and if that does not help it gives that spot up for a while. Press Restart crew in the job site to bring everyone back and try again.

The status line under the job name always says what a site is waiting for. Messages also pop up in the corner of the screen.

Workers never break blocks where you could not, and never touch another player's chests.
